correctness.rationale: The essential-variable locus is the first-catalecticant rank locus and is projective. A diagonal one-parameter subgroup with base-B variable weights, B>d, makes all degree-d monomial weights distinct. For a monomial, first-catalecticant rank equals support size because its nonzero coordinate derivatives are distinct monomials. Thus fixed points of the cumulative locus are exactly monomials with support at most r. Choosing the support and a positive composition of d gives the exact count binomial(m,s) binomial(d-1,s-1). Euler localization gives the cumulative formula and additivity gives the exact-stratum formula. For r>d the fixed count is constant, while Fermat sums show the exact strata remain nonempty. The bundled checker replays all support counts over a broad finite grid.

value.rationale: The number of essential variables is a basic complexity invariant of a homogeneous form and the cumulative loci are natural symmetric subspace varieties. The theorem gives the complete Euler profile of the entire filtration, with an exact combinatorial formula for every cumulative locus and exact stratum. The strongest structural feature is that every nonempty exact stratum of essential dimension greater than the polynomial degree has compactly supported Euler characteristic zero, so the cumulative Euler characteristic reaches the ambient value before the geometric filtration reaches the ambient space whenever m>d.
